verdict_note: Two high findings in web.move_file, the lane's core transaction. F1: a `to` whose folder is a case variant of a linked folder moves the file out of local_root on a case-folding file system. F2: in a moved document, relative references that the site port denies (percent-encoded or non-portable names) are neither re-based nor verified, so the move breaks them silently with complete=true. Two medium findings. F3: an unquoted attribute rewrite can corrupt markup and still pass the graph check. F4: the export's link_broken lists have no cap, so the manifest can grow past the 1 MiB that publish and verify read back. The JobPort admission is otherwise correct. Each web job asks the bound port exactly once (session jobs.rs admit_within: cancel, then stale, then port), before any lock, file read or write; the one exception is the canonicalize call in F5. The resource is never absent and is a valid SDOC id. Every exit path settles the job: the closure result settles it, and on a panic AdmittedJob::drop settles it abandoned. The red tests failed for the stated reasons (red, red2, red3, red4 logs), and focused-3 passed 33/33, including the drive process test. This review ran no cargo, build or test.

findings.severity: high (path escape out of the site root; case-folding gap)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:161-163 (Files::through_link compares exact case); :997-1006 (the `to` checks: through_link with exact case; `taken` checks folders only at the last segment); :1090-1096 (create_dir_all, then rename); :415-417 (the walk records a symlink or junction in Files.links only); :166-178 (Files::moved keeps the requested spelling)
findings.what: The `to` checks compare each path prefix with the walked links and folders in exact case, except the last segment. On a case-folding file system (NTFS, or APFS by default), a `to` whose folder segment is a case variant of a linked folder passes both through_link and `taken`. std::fs::rename then resolves the path through the link, and the file leaves local_root. A case variant of an existing real folder also gets through. On NTFS the file lands in the existing folder, while every reference is rewritten with the other spelling, and the next web.site_report flags those references as case_mismatch. On a case-sensitive file system the same move creates a second folder instead. So the outcome depends on the file system (STU-WEB-131 determinism). The graph check cannot see either case, because Files::moved inserts `to` in the requested spelling.
findings.scenario: site/media is a directory symlink or junction to D:/elsewhere (the walk skips it as `link`). web.move_file {"from": "orphan.png", "to": "MEDIA/orphan.png"}: through_link([MEDIA, orphan.png]) is false because links holds `media`, and taken is false. The rename moves orphan.png to D:/elsewhere/orphan.png, and the receipt says complete=true. Variant: img/ exists. {"from": "orphan.png", "to": "Img/orphan.png"} on NTFS puts the file in img/ and rewrites index.html's reference to "Img/orphan.png", which the next report lists as link_broken case_mismatch.
findings.fix: Fold case in through_link and in `taken` for every prefix of `to`, keying links and folders by their ASCII-lowercase form as Files.folded does. Refuse move_outside_site when a prefix folds to a link. When a prefix folds to an existing folder spelled differently, refuse it or adopt the existing spelling. As a second guard before the rename, require resolved(to_path.parent()) to start with resolved(root), the check Port::resolve already makes (web_commands.rs:875-877). Red tests: a case-variant link (with a junction on Windows, which needs no privilege) and a case-variant folder.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:1148-1153 (plan re-bases only File, Missing, Case and Folder reaches; a Denied reach falls to `continue`); :210 (Reach::place keys a Denied reference by its deny code only); :1028 (the graph comparison); :323 with :284-288 (SitePort denies every path with a non-portable segment)
findings.what: In the moved document, a relative reference that the site port or the engine denies is neither re-based nor refused. Examples are a percent-encoded name, a name that is not portable (such as one with a space), or a path through a linked folder. Verification compares the reference as (4, "not_granted") before and after, so the check passes, and the receipt says complete=true while the reference now resolves against the new folder. The manual's promise that 'every reference must reach the same place' (web_site.rs:45-46) does not hold for denied references. Non-moving documents have the same gap: a denied spelling of `from`, such as `thanks%2Ehtml` (engine ambiguous_path), is never rewritten.
findings.scenario: site/gallery.html holds , and site/photos/Summer 2024.jpg exists (the walk skips it as name_not_portable). web.move_file {"from": "gallery.html", "to": "pages/gallery.html"} keeps src="photos/Summer%202024.jpg", which now names pages/photos/Summer 2024.jpg. The command is not refused, the receipt says complete=true, and the image is broken.
findings.fix: In plan, for the moved document, refuse reference_not_rewritable (naming the document and line) for any relative, non-rooted reference whose reach is Denied, or re-base it by path arithmetic on its unchanged bytes. In Reach::place, key a Denied reference by its folder-resolved raw path rather than its code, so that a change of location is caught. Red test: the gallery scenario above.

findings.severity: medium (silent markup corruption that passes verification)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:1179-1180 (Quote::Unquoted is escaped as if double-quoted, and no quotes are added); hsk-studio-web-core/src/entity.rs:46-58 (escape_attr escapes only &, the active quote and CR); hsk-studio-web-core/src/dom.rs:237-243 (Quote::Unquoted); web_site.rs:1028 (verification compares only the places references reach)
findings.what: When character references moved the reference's offsets, the whole attribute value is rewritten. For an unquoted value, the replacement is escape_attr(value, '"'), written back without quotes. Any ASCII whitespace or '>' that came from a character reference becomes literal, so it ends the value or the tag. The re-parsed reference still reaches the same file, so move_rewrite_unverified does not fire, and the corrupted bytes are written.
findings.scenario: site/index.html holds x. web.move_file {"from": "thanks.html", "to": "pages/thanks.html"} writes x: href becomes "pages/thanks.html?q=a", and a new attribute b appears. With href=thanks.html?x=>y, the tag ends early and the text content changes. In both cases the receipt says complete=true.
findings.fix: For Quote::Unquoted, write '"' + escape_attr(value, '"') + '"' over the value span, or refuse reference_not_rewritable. In verification, also require each rewritten reference to equal the planned reference_after, and every other reference to keep its text. Red test: the scenario above.

findings.severity: medium (unbounded output; publish refuses the lane's own export)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:893-895 and :940-946 (the site export keeps every link_broken row; no cap); web_commands.rs:646-665 (the open export's link_broken has no cap either); web_commands.rs:1040 (read_manifest reads at most MAX_RECORD_BYTES = 1 MiB and maps a larger file to no_export)
findings.what: The export's link_broken list has no MAX_ROWS cap, while the report's rows do. The manifest's size is also never checked against the 1 MiB that web.publish and web.verify read back. A large broken-link list writes a manifest that publish and verify then refuse as no_export, and so does a site export near the 4096-file limit, now that the manifest also carries a documents list. The op record's detail and the result carry every row.
findings.scenario: One page holds 15000 <a href="gone-N.html"> links (the engine allows 200000 references per document). web.export, in open or site mode, writes a manifest with more than 1 MiB of link_broken rows, and web.publish then refuses no_export. Estimate, not run: a 4096-page site export takes about 165 bytes per pretty-printed files row plus about 134 per documents row, about 1.2 MB in all, which is also over the bound.
findings.fix: Cap link_broken at MAX_ROWS, with a link_broken_truncated count in the manifest and the result, as the report does with truncated. Before the first write, refuse export_manifest_too_large when the serialized manifest exceeds MAX_RECORD_BYTES, or raise read_manifest's bound to match. Add a test at the bound.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:741 with :766 (site_resource calls canonicalize before the port is asked); :749 (the settlement is discarded); web_commands.rs:280 (execute refuses a canceled token before admission); web_commands.rs:685 and :722-739 (publish takes no CancellationToken); unit test web_site.rs:1233-1234
findings.what: (a) With no package open, std::fs::canonicalize touches the file system before the port is asked, so a slow network local_root blocks before admission. (b) execute's own check refuses a token that is already canceled, so the lifecycle never counts refused_canceled or emits its frame. The unit test's canceled assertion proves only that pre-check, not the admission's canceled path. (c) The settlement is dropped, so neither the result nor the record carries the ticket, correlation or outcome, unlike as_export_job (harness-view view/layout_export.rs:552). (d) web.publish is now an admitted job but never checks cancellation between files (brief item 7). (e) The parameters of web.move_file and web.publish are read after admission. With a saturated port, a malformed web.move_file therefore answers overloaded, not parameter_missing.
findings.scenario: local_root is on an unreachable SMB share and the port is saturated: web.site_report blocks in canonicalize before it refuses overloaded. Cancel during a 4096-file web.publish: every file is still copied, and the job settles completed.
findings.fix: Derive the site id lexically (std::path::absolute plus case folding, with no file-system call), or compute it once at web.site. Attach job detail to the result in the shape of settlement_json. In publish, check the token per file and settle canceled with the partial receipt. Add a test that binds a lifecycle, cancels, and asserts refused_canceled = 1 and port asked = 0.

findings.certainty: READ (whether the NOT_PROVEN branch ran: RUN-NOT-DONE)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/web_site.rs:420-423 (the test returns PASS when the symlink cannot be made); :306-325 (the move refusal table); :576-614 (the viewer jobs test with a package open never asserts the resource)
findings.what: a_linked_folder_inside_the_site_is_skipped returns early and passes when symlink_dir fails (no Developer Mode or privilege). nextest hides the NOT_PROVEN line on a pass, so focused-3 cannot show whether the test ran (UNVERIFIED). No test moves a file through or into a linked folder (F1). The move refusal table lost its absolute-path case in 0b59d57e (step 0) and has no row for a root-relative /x.png, UNC //host/share/x.png, ADS orphan.png:s, or device names con.png and NUL. The code refuses all of these (site_path web_site.rs:691-698 with portable web_commands.rs:910-919; READ), but no test pins it. The package-open viewer test never asserts that the port saw the package's document id.
findings.scenario: On a machine where symlink_dir fails with ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD, the hostile link test passes without running its checks, a silent green (V4-03).
findings.fix: Use a junction on Windows (no privilege needed), or fail with a NOT_PROVEN marker that lane-check counts. Add the case-variant link move. Build an absolute `to` at runtime from the scratch folder, so no literal is added and step 0 stays clean, and add the UNC, ADS and device-name rows. Assert that the admitted resource equals the opened package's document id.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:651-657 (SiteLock::drop removes the file unconditionally); :677-683 (on contention, the foreign lock file, up to MAX_RECORD_BYTES, is echoed whole into detail.holder)
findings.what: When its guard drops, a holder deletes whatever .studio-site.lock is present. After the documented manual step (delete a stale lock), holder A's guard can delete a new holder B's lock, so a third command runs beside B. On contention, the whole foreign lock file (any JSON up to 1 MiB) is copied into the op record's detail.
findings.scenario: A runs web.move_file and stalls. The operator deletes the lock, and B's web.site_report takes it. A finishes, and its drop removes B's lock. C's web.move_file then runs concurrently with B.
findings.fix: Write a nonce into the lock at each acquisition, and remove the file on drop only if it still holds that nonce. On contention, report only actor.account_id, client_session and command_id, each passed through row_text.

findings.severity: low (undeclared limits and false site-wide blocks)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:477-478 (a style sheet containing </style is unparsed, stylesheet_unreadable); :869-871 and :1010-1012 (any unparsed file makes the site export and every move refuse document_unreadable); :1022 (apply refuses a file that needs more than Limits::max_edits = 1024 edits; hsk-studio-web-core/src/dom.rs:208, source_dom_patch.rs:92)
findings.what: A single style sheet whose comment or string contains </style (legal CSS) makes the site export refuse and every web.move_file refuse, even if that sheet references nothing. A moved page with more than 1024 relative references, or a page with more than 1024 references to `from`, refuses with the engine's limit code. The manual (web_site.rs:6-73) declares neither limit.
findings.scenario: styles/old.css holds /* IE hack: */. web.export with documents: site refuses document_unreadable, and so does web.move_file of any file. Separately, moving a gallery page with 1500 relative to pages/ refuses with the edit limit.
findings.fix: Scan the wrapped sheet with each </style replaced by a same-length substitute, so spans stay valid, or refuse only when the sheet is reached. Declare the 1024-edit bound in the manual and in the commands/web.rs row docs, or apply the edits in chunks.

findings.where: S/builders/lanes/hsk-studio-web-site-1.json:54 (host_integration.jobs is "none"); S/builders/briefs/lane-smb-web-site-1.md:74 (the same block); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:63-71 (the manual's jobs bullet has no deadline statement)
findings.what: The lane now admits four job classes through the JobPort (web.export, web.publish, web.site_report and web.move_file), yet host_integration still declares jobs none. The manual also does not state the deadline class that common rule (6) lists (HBR-HOST-004), as harness-view job_admission.rs:27-33 does for the viewer's job classes.
findings.scenario: A steward who checks host_integration for HBR-HOST-004 coverage skips this lane's jobs.
findings.fix: Set host_integration.jobs to the four classes, with the port, the resource rule and the outcomes. Add a line to the manual such as 'Deadline: none by nature, ended by cancel', or admit through admit_by.

lead_questions: With a package open, web.move_file is admitted as Action::Edit on the package's document id, though the command refuses to touch the package. With no package open, the resource is a hash-derived SDOC id that no Folio document has. Keep both rules, or always admit site work on the site-derived id? Does the host's Job Runtime (kernel-bindings BridgeJobs) accept an unknown SDOC id (NOT_INSPECTED)?
web.save and the open export take no site lock, while web.move_file restores files from in-memory originals when a write fails. Should saving a document inside local_root take the site lock?

A move leaves recipe.file stale when the entry document moves (the next site export refuses entry_document_missing). It also leaves case-mismatched spellings of `from` unrewritten, though they work on the local disk today. Do these belong in this slice or in the change-link-site-wide slice?

One unparsed file anywhere in the site, such as a legacy windows-1252 page or a page over 8 MiB, blocks every web.move_file and the site export. Accept this as fail-closed, or name it in the manual as a declared limit?
checked: The full diff eb17fad6..e3fc0e89 (7 files). All of web_site.rs. In web_commands.rs: execute, open, save, port, export (open mode, link_broken), publish (lock placement), verify, Port::resolve (pages flag), asset_id, portable, resolved, output_names, line_at, checked_path, read_bounded, write_atomic, write_new, read_manifest, recipe_from (documents), recipe_json, run() (package resource, package origin) and Run::bind_web_jobs. In commands/web.rs: the rows and the documents parameter. In harness-view: view/web.rs and job_admission.rs (job_binding). The web_host.rs row-count change.

Brief items mapped to code and tests. Item 1: the fixture and its expectations match a_site_reports_exports_and_moves_as_one_link_graph. Item 2: walk (sorted per folder, ids in a BTreeSet, iterative stack with no recursion; caps of 16384 entries, 4096 files and 32 segments; non-UTF-8 names skipped; links skipped and recorded); SiteSet::load (live open document, 8 MiB per file, 64 MiB and 262144 references per site). Item 3: site_report (rows sorted and capped at MAX_ROWS with truncated, not_checked declared, lock file and reserved names excluded, documents never orphans). Item 4: export_site and the open export's page-link warning; publish reads the manifest unchanged. Item 5: move_file (span edits, link base, re-base, parse and graph check before the first write, atomic writes, rename last, restore with a receipt; not an undo step; open document reopened with a fresh history). Item 6: site_lock (create_new, never waits, names the holder, released by drop on every exit including unwind). Item 7: admitted. Item 8: module docs, rows and manual.

SMB-WEB-SITE-1 rulings. R60 probe j3: with_no_package_open_web_jobs_still_ask_the_bound_port, through_the_viewer::the_probe_j3_export_with_no_package_asks_the_viewers_port and through_the_viewer::web_jobs_are_admitted_through_the_viewers_job_port (saturated port: asked once, nothing written). Accepted decisions present: .css scanning, case_mismatch, output_inside_site, entry_document_missing, move_site_record, move_kind_changes, move_case_only, folder links. move_open_package: from, to, and paths inside the package refused (test a_move_never_touches_the_opened_package).

JobPort. Read session jobs.rs admit_within (order: cancel, deadline, stale, then a port hold only when a resource is set), AdmittedJob::drop (settles abandoned) and AdmissionJobPort. Compared with as_export_job (layout_export.rs:543-561): bound revision equals head in both, so stale_revision cannot fire in either. Only Viewer::web_command and the tests call Run::web_command, and Viewer::web_command rebinds the viewer's port before every command.

Derived resource id. The format passes DomainId::parse (accord lib.rs:251-279: prefix SDOC, 36 characters, '7' at index 14, variant at index 19). It carries about 122 bits of SHA-256, contains no path text, and is stable for one canonical folder.

Path traversal in move. site_path with portable refuses `..`, absolute paths, UNC paths, backslashes, ADS names (':'), device names, leading dots and trailing dots (READ). Moves onto an existing file, case-only renames, reserved names and kind changes are refused before the lock. The exception is the case-folding gap in F1.

Receipts and undo_name. web.site_report and web.move_file have mutates_authority=false, consistent with web.open, web.save and web.export and with the ruling that a move is not a web.undo step. drive.rs web() (:229-250) returns the command's detail with no undo_name key. The F1-class undo_name read (drive.rs:300-307) applies only to typed layout.* rows, so it cannot be dishonest for web rows.
Records rule. The lane deletes no object; move_site_record refuses to move a page that has a sidecar beside it, so no record is orphaned.

Logs. red (0b59d57e): 10/10 failed for the stated reasons (unknown_command, asset_missing, parameter_unknown documents). red2 (dcf46289): 2 failed (the package move was accepted; the viewer's web.export returned Ok through a saturated port). red3 (192012e8): 2 failed (one on a helper, fixed in 629f5fcd). red4 (629f5fcd): 2 failed (export accepted with no package open, port asked 0 times). focused-3 (e3fc0e89): 33/33 passed, including web_host::web_commands_run_in_the_drive_session. The example studio-harness.exe timestamp (11:30 local) falls inside focused-3's run, so the exe was plausibly freshly built.

Portability: no drive-letter, user-profile or font literal in the diff. No change to Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, no new dependency, and no new crate edge (harness-core already depended on hsk-studio-session). beyond_brief_paths records both harness-view files. No doc examples were added.
